subject: Clarification on 'no model training' promise, backups and snapshot retention
messages:
From: Aisha Khan <legal@finservcorp.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Reynolds <security@finservcorp.com>
Date: Mon, 4 May 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Quick Q: Do you train on customer data? backups & snapshots

Hi Kimberly,

As part of our vendor review, we need written clarity on Redwood's statement that you do not train models on customer data. Specifically:

- Does "no training" include any internal re-training, fine-tuning, or automated improvement pipelines that might pick up customer inputs?
- What happens to transient in-memory artifacts (KV/cache, prefix cache) — are any of these ever persisted beyond a single request?
- Do backups, debug snapshots, or forensic snapshots contain customer content? If so, what are retention windows and deletion processes?

We also need to understand the ability to request a bulk purge and the timeline for that. Our security team would like a short matrix showing default retention for logs, snapshots, backups, and customer-requested deletions.

Thanks — appreciate a concrete answer we can include in our security review.

Regards,
Aisha Khan
Senior Counsel, FinServCorp

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Aisha Khan <legal@finservcorp.com>
Cc: Tom Reynolds <security@finservcorp.com>, Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 4 May 2026 13:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Quick Q: Do you train on customer data? backups & snapshots

Hi Aisha — thanks for the clear list. Short answer up front: Redwood does not use customer request or content to train or improve our public models or model weights. Below I outline specifics and a short retention matrix. Mina (ops) and Priyom (privacy) are cc'd for the operational/contract follow-ups.

High-level commitments:
- No training on customer data: We do not use customer-provided prompts, payloads, or generated outputs to fine-tune or retrain our hosted model weights. This applies to both our Redwood-managed hosted models and to the curated open-model catalog we serve.
- Telemetry & aggregated metrics: We collect aggregated telemetry (latency, error rates, token counts) for platform health. These metrics do not contain customer prompt text.

Retention & artefacts:
- In-flight caches (KV cache / prefix cache): Ephemeral, kept only in memory for the active request or session and not written to persistent customer-visible storage. For long-running sessions there is a short-lived in-memory window (seconds to minutes) — nothing in that cache is used to train models.
- Request/response logs: By default, request and response logs are retained for 30 days for debugging and billing. Customers on Dedicated or Private plans can configure shorter windows or opt-out; enterprise contracts can set custom retention.
- Debug snapshots & forensic backups: We take periodic snapshots to support incident investigation and SRE debugging. Those snapshots may contain customer content and are retained for up to 90 days by default; access is strictly limited to a small SRE group and is audited. We can exclude a customer's data from those snapshots for Private deployments or via contractual controls.
- Backups / archival storage: Critical system backups may include customer data if it was persisted to storage; archival backups are retained per our backup policy (90 days default) and are subject to deletion when a formal purge is requested.

Deletion / purge requests:
- Self-service deletion: Customers can delete persisted records via the Console or API. Deleted data is removed from primary stores within 24–72 hours and from most operational caches immediately.
- Bulk purge: For a full account purge (including backups and snapshots), we require a signed request. Once initiated, primary data stores are removed within 72 hours and we schedule deletion from backups/snapshots with a maximum window of 90 days to complete final irrecoverable deletion. We provide a deletion certificate when the purge completes.

Evidence & attestation:
- We maintain a non-training attestation and can provide a signed certificate for procurement/legal: see attachment (redwood_no_train_certificate.pdf).
- Retention matrix attached: retention_matrix_finserv.xlsx.

If you'd like, Mina can provide the SRE playbook excerpt showing access controls and audit logging for snapshot access. Happy to schedule a short call to walk through this with your security team.

Best,
Kimberly Park
Enterprise Account Executive | Redwood Inference
kimberly_park@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0132

From: Tom Reynolds <security@finservcorp.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Aisha Khan <legal@finservcorp.com>
Date: Tue, 5 May 2026 08:17:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Quick Q: Do you train on customer data? backups & snapshots

Kimberly — thanks for the thorough note. A couple quick follow-ups for the SOC/contract review:

1) Can you confirm whether automated anomaly-detection retraining pipelines (internal to Redwood) ever sample production traffic for training candidate datasets?
2) For the 90-day snapshot retention, do you have role-based access logs we can inspect or an SOC2 control we can reference that limits snapshot access?
3) If we ask for a purge today, can you provide an estimated date when backups will be fully scrubbed? We need a date for our procurement schedule.

If you can respond with a slightly more prescriptive timeline for the purge and the SOC2 control ids, that will help us move forward.

—Tom
Director of Security, FinServCorp
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Tom Reynolds <security@finservcorp.com>, Aisha Khan <legal@finservcorp.com>
Cc: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 5 May 2026 15:46:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Quick Q: Do you train on customer data? backups & snapshots

Tom — quick clarifications below, and I’ve attached the two artifacts we mentioned. Priyom and Mina are on the thread if you want more detail.

1) Automated pipelines: No. We do not sample production traffic into any automated model-retraining pipelines. Any modeling work that uses customer data would be done only with explicit opt-in and under a separate contractual agreement.

2) Snapshot access & SOC2: Snapshot access is limited via RBAC; access requests are logged and retained per our audit-logging policy. Our SOC 2 Type II report (control IDs listed in the attached attestation) covers access to backups and change management. I can provide a redacted excerpt of the control matrix under NDA if needed.

3) Purge timeline: If you submit a signed purge request now, primary data deletion completes within 72 hours. Backup/snapshot scrub completes on a rolling schedule with a maximum completion window of 90 days; for your procurement docs you can list an estimated completion date of 2026-08-03 (90 days from acceptance). We will provide a deletion certificate once completed.

Attachments: redwood_no_train_certificate.pdf (signed attestation), retention_matrix_finserv.xlsx (detailed retention per artifact).

Next steps:
- If acceptable, Aisha can confirm the purge process in the contract addendum and we’ll attach the attestation.
- If Tom wants SRE evidence, Mina can schedule a short technical call and share a redacted access log under an NDA.

Thanks — happy to close this out quickly.

Best regards,
Kimberly Park
Enterprise Account Executive | Redwood Inference
